entries.description: Replications of studies evaluating the role of scarcity priming across multiple domains (pain sensitivity, resource allocation, materialism, and others); aggregate results reported for 19 studies without individual study details available in the provided text.
entries.notes: The paper reports 19 replication results aggregated in Fig. 1 and summary text; individual study details (original titles, authors, years, journals, per-study results, and citation sentences) are not available in the provided full text, which is an aggregate summary. The SI Appendix and Fig. 1 would be needed to code each of the 19 entries individually. Four replications (studies 4, 16–18) were reported as significant; the remaining 15 were not. The paper states 'replication effect sizes were smaller than the original effect sizes for 80% of the studies, and directionally opposite for 30% of these 20 studies.' Without individual study breakdowns, each entry is coded as inconclusive with blank fields where the paper does not provide the information.
